name: Portugal: Part II package and CTIS upload check
applies_to: the Portugal package as a whole (plan-level checklist step)

items.check: K1 recruitment and informed-consent procedure on the current EudraLex template, with a section for every population pathway in the plan.
K2 recruitment material present for every recruitment item, each identified by title, version and date.
One Portuguese L1 information and consent set per population in population_sets whose trigger is true, including assent, written age-16 assent and adult re-consent documents where applicable.
Every other participant-facing item (patient cards, instructions, visit schedules, diaries, questionnaires, guides, brochures, appointment information) present in Portuguese.

For every Portuguese site: M1 CV (current, signed, dated), M2 declaration of interests (signed, dated), GCP certificate where needed, N1 site declaration with national detail, service and research-team authorisation, pharmaceutical-services declaration and IMP circuit.
External study coordinator evidence.
External facility documentation, including licensing, insurance extension and financial agreement.
O1 insurer-signed certificate valid at submission, covering every site and external facility, valid during the trial and 12 months after the last participant in Portugal.
O2 evidence of existing civil-liability cover and CEIC acceptance of the dispensation.
P2 financial arrangements for each site (final contract, agreed model or minimum-information document).
P1 reimbursement and compensation description.
Fee handled through the electronic process after submission; no unsupported payment document uploaded.
GDPR-compliance statement in the CTIS Form section covering the Portuguese trial activities (or R1 under Part II if decided).
S1 biological-samples template with Portugal-specific information, consistent with the protocol, participant information and any future-use document.
Portuguese protocol synopsis planned with Part I.
Documents not required by the Clinical Trials Regulation or Portuguese guidance removed.
All participant-facing material and the protocol synopsis are in Portuguese (or a CEIC exceptional waiver is documented).
Other dossier documents are in Portuguese or English.
Investigator CV and declaration of interests, site declaration, service authorisation and insurer certificate are signed and dated where required.
No participant, representative, witness or interviewer signatures in the submitted K and L documents; blank consent forms are not pre-signed.
Language waiver justification submitted to CEIC.
Site names, investigators, team functions and participant estimates identical in CTIS, M1, N1, the service authorisation and P2.
The site declaration includes pharmacy and investigational-product circuit information.
Insurer, policy, cover and damage-compensation wording identical in O1 and every participant document; cover includes every Portuguese site and applicable external facility.
Reimbursement and compensation identical in P1, P2 and every participant document.
Free supply of trial medicines and procedures and the post-trial continuation pathway consistent in P2 and the participant documents.
Data flows, recipients, transfers and retention identical in the GDPR statement, the participant documents and the protocol.
Sample types, storage, transfers and retention identical in S1, the protocol and the participant documents.
Consent pathways in K1 match the L1 sets in the package.
Documents adapted from the reference package contain all Portuguese national additions and no leftovers from the reference country.
items.applies_when: Portugal is not the reference package

items.check: Correct B-S section prefix and CTIS placeholder for each document.
Unique, self-explanatory title of at most 100 characters: <section code>_<document type>_<subtype>_<country>_<language>_<special attribute>, with only the fields that distinguish the document.
Every document title, version and date confirmed against CTIS; version and date in CTIS metadata, not in the title.
Personal names only where disclosure permits (principal investigator in M1/M2).
Clean, tracked-change, redacted or public and split-file variants clearly distinguished.
Uploaded filename base contains none of ( ) / , . ; | [ ] (the period before the extension is fine).
Article 11 workaround: every mandatory Part II placeholder holds the official placeholder PDF titled Part_II_placeholder_document_Article_11_workaround.
items.applies_when: Portugal receives Part I only under Article 11

items.check: For each document, publication status checked against the current Annex I publication tables (revised CTIS transparency rules; ACT EU guidance v2.2, 30 April 2026).
Publishable documents: personal data and CCI identified separately; public version redacts only qualifying material; signatures never disclosed.
CCI redaction only after both tests: not in the public domain, and disclosure would undermine a legitimate economic interest.
No personal data or CCI in public structured fields.
No drafting instruction remains in any document (see content/conventions/template-instructions.md).
Every document approved by the owner in TrialAgents, or the user has explicitly chosen to export unapproved versions.
